newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlots shipping cattle - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlots shipping cattle - feedlots.

text.p: Many cattle sold Tuesday in U.S. Plains feedlot markets started being shipped to meat packing plants Wednesday and more shipments were scheduled Thursday and Friday, feedlot sources said.

Bids from packers were scarce early Thursday, but feedlot managers said the quick shipping schedule has them optimistic packers should be needing to buy more cattle soon. A small number of short-fed cattle traded in Kansas late Wednesday at a steady $66.00 per cwt and were expected to be shipped soon.
Feedlots are extremely current. Many of the cattle sold this week were originally scheduled for sale in January.

Managers said the lower-priced deferred CME live cattle futures contracts encourage feedlots to stay current on marketings. Also, with feeder cattle continually arriving at these feedlots, managers said they need empty pens.
Several managers said there lots are about 90 percent full, which was normal this time of year.
